stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its use in large language model applications.
Key technologies involved include transformers and safetensors, central to modern NLP.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
It pertains to the text-generation pipeline, indicating its application in generative AI tasks.
The model is associated with key ML technologies like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Anthropic will design its own hardware to power Claude
stories.author: Samuel Axon
bullet_points: Anthropic is developing proprietary hardware to support its Claude AI models.
This move signals a strategic effort by major AI labs to reduce reliance on Nvidia GPUs.
The development is part of a broader industry race among AI leaders like Anthropic and OpenAI to scale compute power.

stories.title: Large genome models used to design new viruses
stories.author: John Timmer
bullet_points: Large genome models are being utilized to engineer novel viruses.
The AI system is capable of generating genetically diverse, bacteria-killing viral variants.
This represents a significant application of AI in synthetic biology and virology.

stories.title: New Mexico court orders Meta to pay $567m over harms to children’s mental health
stories.author: boplicity
bullet_points: A New Mexico court has ordered Meta to pay a substantial sum ($567 million) related to harms to children's mental health.
This ruling represents a significant legal and regulatory action targeting major social media platforms regarding youth well-being.
The case highlights growing legal scrutiny on how tech companies design and manage platforms used by minors.

stories.title: AMD acquires Taalas to boost inference performance by etching models in silicon
stories.author: itvision
bullet_points: AMD has acquired Taalas to enhance its capabilities in AI inference.
The core technology involves 'etching models in silicon' to boost inference performance.
This move directly targets the rapidly expanding market for AI inference solutions.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the 'deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1' model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes standard ML components such as transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31 on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is achieved through the implementation of Multi-Token Prediction (MTP) powered by MLX.
Speed improvements reach up to 90% faster when utilized with coding agents, based on the Aider benchmark.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon using the MLX engine.
The performance improvements result in faster response times and lower memory usage for LLMs.
The updated engine also enables models to generate higher quality responses on Apple Silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Introduction of NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra, a new AI model.
The model is specifically designed for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: OpenJarvis: a local-first personal AI is now available to run with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenJarvis v1.0 is released, providing an open-source framework for building personal AI agents.
The framework emphasizes a 'local-first' approach, allowing AI to run entirely on the user's own hardware.
It features built-in support for Ollama, integrating local LLM execution capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama is now powered by MLX on Apple Silicon in preview
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a popular local LLM runner, is integrating MLX for performance gains.
This integration specifically targets Apple Silicon, optimizing AI workloads for Apple hardware.
The feature is currently available in a preview state, indicating ongoing development and optimization.

stories.title: OpenClaw
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: OpenClaw is a new personal AI assistant designed for local execution.
It integrates messaging apps with local AI coding agents.
The core value proposition is running AI processes entirely on the user's own device for privacy/control.

stories.title: Meta ordered to pay an additional $567 million in public nuisance ruling
stories.author: Jess Weatherbed
bullet_points: Meta has been ordered to pay an additional $567 million in a New Mexico public nuisance case.
The ruling found Meta's platforms are a 'significant contributing cause' of teen mental health issues.
This decision significantly increases the total financial liability against Meta in this landmark child safety case.

stories.title: On-Policy Self-Distillation without Any Supervision
stories.author: Nuno Vasconcelos
bullet_points: Introduces a novel method for On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPD) in Large Language Models (LLMs).
Addresses a key limitation of existing methods by removing reliance on external supervision (ground-truth or external guidance).
Achieves 'self'-distillation solely by leveraging the model's own generations and internal consistency.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements.
Enhanced GGUF model compatibility is now supported via llama.cpp.
The update expands model support across various hardware, augmenting the MLX engine on Apple silicon.

stories.title: Subagents and web search in Claude Code
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for subagents within Claude Code.
The update also enables web search capabilities within the Claude Code environment.
This suggests an enhancement in the complexity and capability of AI agents managed via Ollama.

stories.title: Jony Ive’s first OpenAI gadget is reportedly a hockey puck-sized smart speaker
stories.author: Stevie Bonifield
bullet_points: OpenAI is collaborating with Jony Ive on a new AI gadget.
The device is described as a battery-powered, hockey puck-sized smart speaker without a display.
It is anticipated to launch in 2027 with a price point exceeding $300.

stories.title: Suno shares plans to combat spammy AI music
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Suno is introducing watermarking technology to combat the spread of spammy AI-generated music.
The company is also implementing a new download policy to enhance transparency regarding AI tracks.
The move reflects Suno's efforts to gain legitimacy within the rapidly evolving AI music industry.

stories.title: Brendan Carr officially unleashes broadcast consolidation
stories.author: Lauren Feiner
bullet_points: The FCC has voted to eliminate the national broadcast ownership cap rule.
Chair Brendan Carr and Commissioner Olivia Trusty were key proponents of ending the cap.
This decision signals a major shift allowing for greater consolidation among broadcast station owners.

stories.title: Suno hopes to go legit with watermarks for AI-generated music
stories.author: Ryan Whitwam
bullet_points: Suno, an AI music generator, is implementing watermarking technology.
The goal of the watermarks and download limits is to curb 'large-scale abuse' of the platform.
This move signals an industry trend toward addressing copyright and misuse in generative AI.

stories.title: Blue Origin narrowing in on root cause of catastrophic rocket accident
stories.author: Eric Berger
bullet_points: Blue Origin is investigating the cause of a recent catastrophic rocket accident.
The investigation has narrowed the anomaly's origin to the main oxygen valve.
The affected component is located on one of the BE-4 engines.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a framework to allow models to appropriately weigh context.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark for evaluating context-dependent reasoning.

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: The paper addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, which consumes 39-45% of data scientists' time.
It focuses specifically on heart failure, a major health issue requiring integration of fragmented EHR data with clinical guidelines.
The proposed pipeline aims to improve upon existing rule-based and LLM approaches by offering better automation and evidence traceability.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a new method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of current evaluation methods, which either overspend or fail to reach conclusive results.
Provides a certified anytime-valid stopping mechanism, ensuring evaluation stops as soon as sufficient evidence is gathered while maintaining statistical guarantees.

stories.title: The Low Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping
stories.author: Furong Huang
bullet_points: Existing video language models struggle with precise event bookkeeping (counting, timing) due to limitations in real-world benchmarks.
The paper introduces 'trace-grounded parametric profiling' to improve event counting accuracy in controlled video tasks.
This method addresses a gap where current benchmarks only score the final answer instead of auditing reported events against ground truth.

stories.title: Challenges in Evaluating Explanation Methods for Static and Evolving Data
stories.author: Jerzy Stefanowski
bullet_points: The paper addresses critical limitations in evaluating Explainable AI (XAI) methods, particularly concerning insufficient evaluation standards.
It demonstrates challenges using the DetoxAI system for bias detection and concept unlearning in image recognition.
The research explores adapting explanation techniques, such as counterfactuals, to handle concept drift in evolving data streams.

stories.title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
stories.author: Juanzi Li
bullet_points: Introduces TRAJDEBUG, a method designed to trace the error lifecycle in long-horizon agent trajectories.
Addresses a key challenge in LLM-based agentic systems: identifying the earliest root cause of cascading failures.
Focuses on the difficulty of error detection when evidence is scattered across distant steps in complex, long sequences.

stories.title: Tytan: Interactive Neurosymbolic Construction of Analytic Semantic Schemas from Relational Data
stories.author: Kristian J. Hammond
bullet_points: Introduces TYTAN, a system designed to automatically construct analytic semantic schemas from relational data.
Addresses the 'knowledge-acquisition bottleneck' where data understanding (entities, measures, relationships) is currently done manually.
Aims to improve scalability and reduce dependency on domain experts for data analysis tools.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: Addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
Proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simple context resistance.
Introduces MIST, a new human-annotated benchmark for evaluating selective trust in reasoning.

stories.title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
stories.author: Priyadarshini Kachroo
bullet_points: The research addresses the significant bottleneck of EHR feature engineering in clinical AI, which consumes 39-45% of data scientists' time.
The focus is on heart failure, a critical condition requiring the integration of fragmented EHR data with complex, guideline-based clinical reasoning.
The proposed pipeline aims to improve upon existing rule-based and LLM approaches by providing evidence-linked and more maintainable automation.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for cost-effective evaluation of AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the challenge of unknown game counts in agent comparison, overcoming limitations of fixed-budget evaluations.
Provides a certified anytime-valid stopping mechanism, ensuring evaluation integrity without unnecessary computation.

stories.title: CalibForge: Adversarial Solver Calibration for Scaling Learnable Terminal Tasks
stories.author: Kai Jia
bullet_points: Introduces CalibForge, a system for autonomous synthesis of terminal tasks for learning agents.
The system uses adversarial solver calibration to ensure generated tasks are appropriately challenging, not just solvable.
Addresses the gap between task feasibility (executability) and task difficulty relative to a specific solver setting.

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a limitation in applying generative reward models (GRMs) to Reinforcement Learning (RL).
The core issue identified is the mismatch between GRM's comparative nature and RL's scalar scoring requirement.
The authors propose a novel method (RRC) to bridge this gap, enabling GRMs to be effectively used in LLM RL.

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: The paper introduces HarnessOpt-Bench, a new benchmark for evaluating Large Language Models (LLMs) within agentic systems.
It highlights that LLM performance is heavily dependent on the 'harness' (prompts, tools, control flow, etc.), not just the model weights.
The work addresses the need for automated harness optimization—using AI to iteratively improve the surrounding system components.

stories.title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
stories.author: Lingdong Kong
bullet_points: The paper addresses the vulnerability of language models to misleading external context signals.
It proposes 'selective trust' as a solution, moving beyond simple context resistance.
MIST is introduced as a new human-annotated benchmark to evaluate context-dependent reasoning.

stories.title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
stories.author: Vamse Kumar Subbiah
bullet_points: The paper investigates programmatic tool calling (PTC) as an advanced method for LLMs to act beyond training data, contrasting it with native JSON tool calling.
PTC allows code-capable models to chain and parallelize actions using scripts, offering a more natural extension than rigid JSON structures.
The research addresses a gap by empirically comparing PTC against native JSON tools on established benchmarks under real-world task conditions.

stories.title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
stories.author: Longbo Huang
bullet_points: Introduces AV-AIVAT, a method for evaluating AI agents in imperfect-information games.
Addresses the inefficiency of traditional evaluations by allowing stopping as soon as sufficient evidence is gathered.
Provides a certified guarantee for the evaluation's validity, overcoming limitations of fixed-budget or naive stopping methods.

stories.title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
stories.author: Shujian Huang
bullet_points: The research addresses the challenge of multilingual reasoning transfer in Large Language Models (LLMs), particularly for low-resource languages.
It introduces RP-OPSD, a novel method that modifies On-Policy Self-Distillation (OPSD) to explicitly prioritize reasoning signals.
The core contribution is characterizing that target-language reasoning involves generating specific structural elements (surfaces/structures) beyond simple surface-level text.

stories.title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
stories.author: Abigail Goldsteen
bullet_points: The paper addresses the critical issue of poor quality in existing benchmarks used to evaluate task-oriented conversational agents.
It introduces a novel, reference-free framework that utilizes Large Language Model (LLM) judges to assess benchmark quality.
The framework provides actionable diagnostics regarding benchmark consistency, complexity, and policy coverage.

stories.title: Benchmarking and Enhancing LLMs for Rule-Intensive Review of National Standard Documents
stories.author: Tianyong Hao
bullet_points: The paper addresses the gap in evaluating LLMs for complex, rule-intensive document review tasks.
National standard documents (e.g., China GB/T) are proposed as a challenging testbed due to their length and strict structural rules.
Current LLM benchmarks are criticized for focusing too much on domain knowledge and QA, neglecting intrinsic rule adherence.

stories.title: RRC: Unlocking Generative Reward Models in LLM Reinforcement Learning via Ranking-Based Reward Construction
stories.author: Jingbo Zhu
bullet_points: The paper addresses a gap in LLM Reinforcement Learning (RL) regarding the underutilization of generative reward models.
It identifies a core limitation: the mismatch between generative models' comparative nature and RL's scalar scoring requirement.
The authors propose a method (RRC) to bridge this gap, enabling generative reward models to be effectively used in RL.

stories.title: Beyond Top-K: Replacing Black-Box Retrieval with Interpretable Agentic Operations
stories.author: Tabarakul Hazarika
bullet_points: Challenges the standard Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) approach (chunking and top-K retrieval) for long documents.
Argues the standard RAG design is structurally unsound for complex, structured documents like financial statements and audit reports.
Proposes replacing black-box retrieval with more interpretable, agentic operations to handle data density issues (e.g., tables and near-identical figures).

stories.title: HarnessOpt-Bench: Evaluating LLMs at Harness Optimization
stories.author: Yuan Xue
bullet_points: The performance of Large Language Models (LLMs) in agentic systems is heavily dependent on the surrounding 'harness' (prompts, tools, control flow, etc.), not just the model weights.
The paper introduces 'HarnessOpt-Bench,' a framework for evaluating automated harness optimization—the use of AI to iteratively improve the surrounding system components.
A key gap identified is the lack of a common protocol within the community for measuring and standardizing harness optimization capabilities.

stories.title: LLM Citation Study Shows Why Publishers Need to Front-Load Their Most Valuable Content
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: LLMs exhibit a strong tendency to cite content found at the beginning of a webpage.
This study suggests a practical implication for content strategy, favoring front-loading valuable information.
The finding highlights a behavioral bias in how current LLMs process and reference web data.

stories.title: Google Search Console Expands to YouTube and Social Channel Performance Data
stories.author: alifar
bullet_points: Google Search Console is expanding its functionality beyond traditional website monitoring.
The expansion introduces experimental platform properties to track performance on YouTube and social channels.
This move integrates cross-platform performance data into a unified Google tool.
